chunks: Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

He was asked about a Bukhti camel that became enraged, went out from the house, and killed a man. Then the man's brother came and struck the stud camel with a sword, crippling it. So he عليه السلام said: "The owner of the Bukhti camel is liable for the blood money, and he receives the price of his camel."

key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: blood money due for unlawful killing
key_terms.بُخْتِيٍّ: a large pack camel of the Bukhti type
key_terms.ثَمَنَ بُخْتِيِّهِ: the price or monetary value of his camel
key_terms.فَعَقَرَهُ: he hamstrung or severely injured it

ai.seo_question: Who is liable if an enraged camel kills someone in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about liability when an enraged camel kills a person. The owner of the camel must pay the diyah, while the animal’s value is owed back to him after it was struck and injured by the victim’s brother.
